decisionSummary: Task 5.3 passes its bounded local fal queue contract. Tasks 6.3 and 6.4 are not eligible for PASS because canonical alias lookup can cross-pair object kind and external ID, tenant/customer hints are not checked against an existing canonical order, and failed inbox deliveries are never retried on redelivery.
whyNotHigherLayer: The billing specification explicitly requires event alias convergence, mismatched mappings to become recovery cases, durable duplicate-delivery handling, and atomic reconciliation. The observed defects are in the runtime query and delivery-control flow; changing only the specification or evidence would leave the unsafe behavior intact.

findings.description: findCanonicalOrderId filters objectKind and externalId with independent IN predicates. For aliases (checkout_session, cs1) and (payment_intent, pi1), rows (checkout_session, pi1) or (payment_intent, cs1) can match even though neither row is one of the supplied alias pairs. This can resolve an event to the wrong canonical order.
findings.requiredEvidence: Exact tuple matching or an equivalent query, plus a regression proving cross-pairs are rejected or become recovery cases.

findings.description: When an alias resolves an existing order, resolveOrder returns that order without checking incoming workspaceId or customerId. reconcilePayment locks input.workspaceId before resolution. A known order from workspace B combined with a workspace/customer hint for A can lock A, mutate order B, and attach aliases without rejecting the mismatch.
findings.requiredEvidence: Tenant and customer mismatch tests demonstrating a conflict/recovery result and no cross-workspace economic effect.

findings.description: Any existing inbox row is returned as duplicate, regardless of whether its status is failed. If reconciliation fails after the row is recorded, a verified redelivery cannot retry the failed economic reconciliation and the event remains permanently failed.
findings.requiredEvidence: A failed-row redelivery test showing safe retry, stable event identity, and no duplicate grant after eventual success.

blocked: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/probe-billing-reconciliation.ts: PostgreSQL CREATEDB permission denied (42501) in the current environment; prior isolated 5/5 probe remains referenced but was not reproduced in this run.

limits: Local fixture provider only; no Stripe account, live fal request, production email, production billing, paid request, or external network evidence.
This review does not approve the M4 or M5 stage gate and does not alter task or stage status.
